1) RUNNING ORDER-NUMBER PER CUSTOMER NUMBERED 1,2,3 IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date)` — ASC, no DESC) — FINDABLE / DOCS-VERIFIED CORRECT.
   • r27:1626 verbatim worked example: `SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY created_at) AS rn` — exact ASC form, no DESC, no NULLS clause needed; ordering oldest→newest. r27:1639, r27:1651 repeat the same pattern in three different rewrite contexts.
   • r23:996 verbatim docs-quote: `ROW_NUMBER() — "Returns a unique, sequential number for each row, starting with one, according to the ordering of rows within the window partition." Sequence with three rows where the top two tie on amount = (100, 100, 80) DESC: 1, 2, 3 (unique — arbitrary tie-break among the two 100s).` Directly lands the 1, 2, 3 enumeration semantic.
   • r07:2042 primitive-table row: `ROW_NUMBER() — assigns a strictly increasing integer (1, 2, 3, 4) within the partition. Ties break arbitrarily.` Plain-English summary of the running-counter behavior.
   • r23:991 decision-table row for the Nth-positioned record use case: `The literal Nth row / Nth-ranked record per group (a specific runner-up row — pick exactly one row at position N, ties broken arbitrarily or by a deterministic tiebreaker) | ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY x DESC, <tiebreaker>) = N | ROW_NUMBER = unique 1, 2, 3, 4 — every row gets a different number, so = N ALWAYS returns exactly one row per group (assuming the partition has N+ rows).` For the running-counter version (label every order with its 1, 2, 3, ... position), drop the `= N` filter and project `rn` itself.
   • COMPOSITION for SAID question (label each customer's orders 1, 2, 3 in chronological order): `SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) AS order_seq FROM iceberg.analytics.orders` — 1-step compose from r27:1626 (exact ASC form already canonical). The first order in time gets rn=1, second gets rn=2, etc. No NULLS clause needed since the canonical r27:1626 form omits NULLS direction (and the r27 LEADING CANONICAL Oracle-vs-Trino NULLS-default block already covers the rare DESC + NULL case).
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via trino.io/docs/current/functions/window.html — quoted in resource at r23:996): `Returns a unique, sequential number for each row, starting with one, according to the ordering of rows within the window partition.` Findable, docs-correct. No edits needed.

2) EACH PAYMENT METHOD'S SHARE AS PERCENT OF TOTAL TRANSACTIONS (one row per method, share = count_per_method / grand_total — `SELECT method, COUNT(*), 100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER ()` OR `100.0 * count_per_method / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t)` subquery form) — FINDABLE / DOCS-VERIFIED CORRECT.
   • r07:1263 LEADING CANONICAL DECISION-ROW (verbatim): `"What percent of total X does EACH bucket contribute?" — one row per bucket | SELECT bucket, SUM(x) * 100.0 / SUM(SUM(x)) OVER () FROM t GROUP BY bucket — see the per-group share card just above.` This is the EXACT shape of the SAID question with `bucket = payment_method` and the metric being `COUNT(*)` instead of `SUM(x)`. The window-over-aggregate `SUM(SUM(x)) OVER ()` generalizes verbatim to `SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER ()` per the r07:1626 docs-quote `All Aggregate functions can be used as window functions by adding the OVER clause` (verified verbatim at trino.io/docs/current/functions/window.html).
   • r07:1262 sibling decision-row for the SINGLE-SUBSET variant: `"What percent of total X comes from a single subset (top quintile / flagged / churned)?" — one scalar answer | Single-pass: SUM(x) FILTER (WHERE subset_pred) * 100.0 / SUM(x)` — the alternative shape when the answer is one number per subset rather than one row per category.
   • r07:1264 sibling decision-row for the rows-preserved variant: `"Show every customer with their % of total" — rows preserved | SUM(x) OVER () window form (see the share-of-grand-total card just above — empty OVER () keeps detail rows).` The three Pareto/share-family rows are all in the same decision cheat-sheet (r07:1258-1265) so the responder routes correctly by question shape.
   • r07:1170+ LEADING CANONICAL for share-of-grand-total with comprehensive keyword anchors `percent of total, share of grand total, each row as a fraction of the total, ratio to total, % of total revenue, contribution to total, what portion of the total, normalize to total, SUM OVER no partition, empty OVER clause, grand-total denominator, pct of overall.` Findability is solid for `share`, `percent`, `fraction`, `ratio`, `% of total` keywords.
   • r07:1190 INTEGER-DIVISION GUARDRAIL: `revenue / SUM(...) on two integers does integer division (truncates to 0). Multiply by the DECIMAL literal 100.0 (or CAST the numerator) so the division is done in floating/decimal — see resource 23 §3 integer-division trap. Wrap in ROUND(..., 2) for a clean percentage.` Pre-empts the most common off-by-zero bug.
   • COMPOSITION for SAID question: `SELECT payment_method, COUNT(*) AS txn_count, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY pct_of_total DESC` — 1-step compose from r07:1263 with `SUM(x) → COUNT(*)`. Alternative subquery form: `SELECT payment_method, COUNT(*) AS txn_count, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions), 2) AS pct_of_total FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions GROUP BY payment_method ORDER BY pct_of_total DESC` — also valid (single CTE-like subquery in the denominator; one extra scan but simpler to read). Both produce identical results; the window-over-aggregate form scans the table once.
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via trino.io/docs/current/functions/window.html): `All Aggregate functions can be used as window functions by adding the OVER clause` — directly authorizes `SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER ()` as the grand-total-of-bucket-counts denominator. Match verified. No edits needed.

3) FIRST AND LAST STATUS PER TICKET IN ONE ROW (`min_by(status, ts)` for first + `max_by(status, ts)` for last — one row per ticket) — FINDABLE / DOCS-VERIFIED CORRECT.
   • r23:636 LEADING CANONICAL Quick-route anchor (iter638 PIN) — explicit verbatim mention of the SAID question shape: `Reach for the min_by(x, y) / max_by(x, y) worked example below ONLY when you want a DIFFERENT column's value AS OF the earliest / latest timestamp (e.g. "the status at the earliest update and the status at the latest update per order" — min_by(status, updated_at) AS first_status, max_by(status, updated_at) AS latest_status).` This is the EXACT shape of the SAID question with `order → ticket` and `updated_at → ts` (same semantic — earliest/latest timestamp per entity, return a non-timestamp column's value as of those bounds).
   • r23:643-644 worked example verbatim: `max_by(status, updated_at) AS latest_status, min_by(status, updated_at) AS first_status` — direct match for the SAID question.
   • r23:632-633 docs-quote signatures: `max_by(x, y) -> [same as x] — "Returns the value of x associated with the maximum value of y over all input values." (Trino docs verbatim.)` + `min_by(x, y) -> [same as x] — symmetric: value of x paired with the MIN of y.`
   • r23:650 worked-example mnemonic: `This is the canonical "value as of latest event" idiom — much shorter than a window-function + QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() = 1 pattern (and QUALIFY does not exist in Trino 467 anyway).`
   • r23:652 sibling DO-NOT-WRITE inoculation (iter573 PIN): never reach for `MAX(status)` to mean "status at latest timestamp" — `MAX` returns the lexicographically/numerically largest, not the most recent. Cross-applies to the SAID question (a responder asked for "last status" might wrongly write `MAX(status)`).
   • COMPOSITION for SAID question: `SELECT ticket_id, min_by(status, updated_at) AS first_status, max_by(status, updated_at) AS last_status FROM iceberg.support.ticket_history GROUP BY ticket_id` — direct lift from r23:643-644 with `order → ticket`. ONE row per ticket, TWO columns. Both first and last in a single GROUP BY pass — no self-join, no window function, no subquery.
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch at trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html): `max_by(x, y)` returns "the value of x associated with the maximum value of y"; `min_by(x, y)` returns "the value of x associated with the minimum value of y". Signatures match r23:632-633 verbatim. The 3-arg variants `max_by(x, y, n) → array<[same as x]>` and `min_by(x, y, n) → array<[same as x]>` exist for top/bottom N. No edits needed.

4) ROUND TO 2 DECIMALS vs TRUNCATE TO 2 DECIMALS (`round(x, 2)` is HALF_UP away-from-zero; `truncate(x*100)/100` is toward zero; Trino's `truncate` is 1-arg ONLY — no 2-arg `truncate(x, d)` overload exists) — FINDABLE / DOCS-VERIFIED CORRECT.
   • r27:1143-1145 EXPLICIT 3-row mapping table for Oracle → Trino rewrite: `TRUNC(n, d) (numeric truncation to d decimal places — Oracle) | truncate(n * power(10, d)) / power(10, d) — lowercase 1-arg truncate. For 2 decimals: truncate(n*100)/100. If HALF_UP rounding is acceptable, round(n, d) is simpler (but round is rounding, NOT truncation — they differ at the half-way mark and for negative numbers).` Plus `TRUNC(n) → truncate(n)` 1-arg toward-zero, plus `ROUND(n, d) → round(n, d) — same name, same signature, same HALF_UP semantics. Direct 1:1.`
   • r27:1300-1301 sibling table row repeats the same mapping with `truncate(n)` (1-arg toward zero) and emphasizes `Trino's truncate is 1-arg only; the 2-arg truncate(n, d) form does NOT exist in Trino 467.`
   • r27:1312-1320 worked tax-calc example showing the side-by-side: `SELECT truncate(price * 1.0875 * 100) / 100 AS price_with_tax FROM orders;` (Trino truncation idiom for 2dp) vs `SELECT round(price * 1.0875, 2) AS price_with_tax FROM orders;` with the note `round() is HALF_UP rounding semantics. For most billing/accounting, truncation may be specified by tax authorities; verify before substituting round() for truncate(x*100)/100.`
   • r27:1327-1335 DO-NOT-WRITE matrix with 5 inoculations: (1) `TRUNC(...)` uppercase → `Function 'trunc' not registered` name-miss; (2) `truncate(n, d)` 2-arg → `Unexpected parameters (decimal(...), integer) for function truncate. Expected: truncate(<numeric type>)` wrong-arity; (3) `TRUNCATE(x)` uppercase confusion with `TRUNCATE TABLE` DDL; (4) `TRUNC(dt)` for date truncation → use `date_trunc('day', dt)` (different function family); (5) silent substitution of `round(n, d)` for `TRUNC(n, d)` without verifying rounding-vs-truncation is acceptable.
   • r27:1335 EXPLICIT TIE-CASE WORKED EXAMPLE (verbatim): `round(1.235, 2) = 1.24; truncate(1.235 * 100) / 100 = 1.23.` For negative numbers: `round(-1.235, 2) = -1.24; truncate(-1.235 * 100) / 100 = -1.23.` Shows the difference at the halfway mark and for negatives — the two semantic axes where they diverge.
   • r27:1337 KEYWORD-TRAP MEMORIZATION PHRASE (verbatim): `Anyone who writes TRUNC(x, 2) for Trino is using Oracle syntax — Trino has lowercase truncate(x) 1-arg only; to truncate to 2 decimals use truncate(x*100)/100 or (if HALF_UP is OK) round(x, 2).`
   • r23:558 sibling lock confirms round semantics: `ROUND(x, n) on Trino is also HALF_UP (verified at trino.io/docs/current/functions/math.html — round(x, d) rounds to d decimal places). It produces the same result as the CAST in HALF_UP terms; it does NOT give you a banker's-rounding option. Trino has no built-in HALF_EVEN cast function.`
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch at trino.io/docs/current/functions/math.html): `truncate(x)` — "Returns x rounded to integer by dropping digits after decimal point." 1-arg ONLY. `round(x)` — "Returns x rounded to the nearest integer." `round(x, d)` — "Returns x rounded to d decimal places." The docs page does NOT explicitly publish the rounding mode for `round(x, d)`; resource 23 §3.1C documents (via Trino source: `core/trino-spi/.../DecimalConversions.java` and `core/trino-main/.../DecimalCasts.java` both use `setScale(..., HALF_UP)`) that Trino's casts and rounding consistently use HALF_UP (round half away from zero), NOT banker's. Resource framing is source-verified-correct; the docs page is silent on the mode but the source is authoritative. No edits needed.

5) COUNT OF DISTINCT (country, city) MULTI-COLUMN PAIRS (Trino REJECTS `COUNT(DISTINCT (col1, col2))` — use `COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(col1, col2))` or pre-concat to a single key) — FINDABLE / DOCS-VERIFIED CORRECT.
   • r23:116 LEADING INOCULATION (verbatim): `"Use COUNT(DISTINCT (col1, col2)) to count distinct pairs" — Trino requires a function-style call; the supported form for distinct PAIRS is COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(col1, col2)) (or pre-concat to a single key). The multi-column-distinct discussion above is about MULTIPLE INDEPENDENT distinct aggregates on different columns, not about composite-key DISTINCT.` This is the DIRECT docs-truth for the SAID question, plus the routing to `ROW(...)` constructor syntax.
   • r23:77-116 §3 LEADING CANONICAL block for the SIBLING question shape (multiple INDEPENDENT distinct aggregates on DIFFERENT columns) explicitly contrasts the two shapes so the responder doesn't confuse them: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), COUNT(DISTINCT session_id), COUNT(DISTINCT page_url) FROM events` is the multi-INDEPENDENT-distinct shape (three separate cardinalities); `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(country, city)) FROM addresses` is the composite-key shape (one cardinality of the (country, city) tuple).
   • COMPOSITION for SAID question: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(country, city)) AS distinct_country_city_pairs FROM iceberg.analytics.addresses` — direct lift from r23:116. Alternative: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT country || '|' || city) AS distinct_pairs FROM iceberg.analytics.addresses` (pre-concat with a delimiter that cannot appear in either field; the `|` delimiter is safe for country/city names which don't contain `|`). Both produce identical results when the inputs are non-null and the delimiter is collision-free; the `ROW(...)` form is safer because it does not depend on a delimiter being absent from the data. THIRD alternative: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT country, city FROM addresses) t` — explicit subquery form, also equivalent.
   • r23:124 sibling note explains the performance implication of `COUNT(DISTINCT)` in general: `For a query like SELECT event_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events GROUP BY event_date, Trino first shuffles rows partitioned by the GROUP BY key (event_date) so different workers handle different days. Then, for each distinct column, it performs an additional shuffle partitioned by (event_date, user_id) so duplicate user_ids land on the same worker and can be deduplicated. This is the MarkDistinct strategy.` Same MarkDistinct cost applies to `COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(country, city))` — Trino shuffles by the ROW key. Findable and explained.
   • DOCS-TRUTH (verified 2026-06-08 via WebFetch at trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html): the COUNT page does not enumerate the multi-column distinct shape directly (the page covers single-arg `count(x)` and `count(*)`), so the `COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(a, b))` idiom is a community-known Trino composition (ROW constructor + COUNT DISTINCT). The resource correctly flags that `COUNT(DISTINCT (a, b))` (parens-as-tuple, not the explicit `ROW(...)` constructor) is REJECTED by Trino's analyzer because parentheses there are treated as a grouped scalar expression, not a tuple constructor. ROW(a, b) is the docs-canonical multi-field constructor (per Trino types page: ROW is a structural type with `ROW(field1 type1, field2 type2, ...)` syntax). Match verified. No edits needed.

6) TRIMMED-MEAN EXCLUDING TOP/BOTTOM 5% (`approx_percentile` for the 5%/95% bounds + `AVG(...) WHERE x BETWEEN p5 AND p95` filter) — SYNTHESIZABLE-FROM-PRIMITIVES WATCH-ITEM (NOT pre-probed per directive).
   • Primitives all individually findable: r23:141-165 covers `approx_percentile(x, 0.05)` and `approx_percentile(x, ARRAY[0.05, 0.95])` (multi-percentile-in-one-pass form). r23:163 verbatim: `approx_percentile(x, percentages) -> array<[same as x]> — multiple percentiles in ONE pass, returns an array aligned to the input ARRAY[...] (e.g. ARRAY[0.5, 0.95, 0.99]). Always prefer this over running three separate approx_percentile calls — one sketch, one shuffle, three numbers out.` Findable for the bounds computation.
   • COMPOSITION for SAID question (NOT pre-probed — directive holds as WATCH-ITEM): `WITH bounds AS (SELECT approx_percentile(amount, ARRAY[0.05, 0.95]) AS pcts FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions) SELECT AVG(t.amount) AS trimmed_mean_5pct FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions t, bounds b WHERE t.amount BETWEEN b.pcts[1] AND b.pcts[2]` — composes from approx_percentile primitive (r23:163 ARRAY form, returns 1-indexed array per Trino convention) + standard `BETWEEN ... AND ...` predicate + bounds-CTE pattern + `AVG(...)` aggregate. Element indexing on Trino arrays is 1-based: `pcts[1]` = 5th percentile, `pcts[2]` = 95th percentile.
   • Alternative form using FILTER: `SELECT AVG(amount) FILTER (WHERE amount BETWEEN (SELECT approx_percentile(amount, 0.05) FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions) AND (SELECT approx_percentile(amount, 0.95) FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions)) AS trimmed_mean FROM iceberg.analytics.transactions` — two subqueries for the bounds (each scans the table once for percentile computation), then filter the AVG. Slightly less efficient than the CTE form (two extra scans for the subqueries vs one for the CTE) but simpler to read.
   • WATCH-ITEM RATIONALE: Per the iter655 directive, the trimmed-mean composition is SYNTHESIZABLE-FROM-PRIMITIVES (approx_percentile + BETWEEN + AVG are all r23/r07-documented separately). Do NOT manufacture pre-probe content. If a future probe specifically asks for `trimmed mean` / `winsorized average` / `5% trimmed mean` and the responder cannot find the bounds-then-filter composition (or surfaces a non-existent `trimmed_mean()` aggregate), then add a 1-card worked example to r23 §3 or r07 §1a. Until then, HOLD as WATCH-ITEM.

=== DOCS-TRUTH SUMMARY (verified 2026-06-08 via trino.io/docs/current via WebFetch) ===
• ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) — `Returns a unique, sequential number for each row, starting with one, according to the ordering of rows within the window partition.` Strictly increasing 1, 2, 3, ... per partition. ASC ordering numbers oldest→newest; DESC numbers newest→oldest. ✓ (matches r23:996 + r07:2042 + r27:1626 verbatim)
• SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () — `All Aggregate functions can be used as window functions by adding the OVER clause.` Authorizes wrapping COUNT(*) in SUM(...) OVER () for the grand-total-of-bucket-counts denominator in the percent-of-total / share-of-total decision-table row (r07:1263). ✓ (matches r07:1626 verbatim)
• max_by(x, y) / min_by(x, y) — `Returns the value of x associated with the maximum/minimum value of y over all input values.` Two-arg form for the canonical "value of column X as of latest/earliest timestamp Y per group" idiom. 3-arg variants for top/bottom N. ✓ (matches r23:632-633 + r23:643-644 verbatim)
• round(x, d) — `Returns x rounded to d decimal places.` Mode not docs-published but source-verified HALF_UP (round half away from zero) per Trino's DecimalConversions.java and DecimalCasts.java (both use `setScale(..., HALF_UP)`). `round(1.235, 2) = 1.24`. ✓ (matches r23:558 + r27:1145 + r27:1335)
• truncate(x) — `Returns x rounded to integer by dropping digits after decimal point.` 1-arg ONLY (no 2-arg `truncate(x, d)` overload exists). For 2dp truncation: `truncate(x*100)/100`. Toward-zero semantics: `truncate(-1.235 * 100) / 100 = -1.23` (NOT `-1.24` as HALF_UP would give). ✓ (matches r27:1143-1145, 1300-1301, 1335 verbatim)
• COUNT(DISTINCT ROW(a, b)) — multi-column distinct PAIR count idiom. `COUNT(DISTINCT (a, b))` parens-as-tuple is REJECTED (Trino treats parens as grouped scalar expression, not tuple constructor); must use explicit `ROW(a, b)` constructor. Alternative: pre-concat with collision-free delimiter `COUNT(DISTINCT a || '|' || b)`. ✓ (matches r23:116 verbatim)
• approx_percentile(x, ARRAY[0.05, 0.95]) → array<[same as x]> — multi-percentile-in-one-pass form, 1-indexed array result. Composes with `AVG(...) WHERE x BETWEEN bounds[1] AND bounds[2]` for trimmed-mean. ✓ (matches r23:163 verbatim)
